references.text: In the Sermon on the Mount, Jesus gives corresponding teaching on divorce and remarriage, where he says that whoever divorces his wife for any reason other than sexual immorality causes her to commit adultery, and whoever marries a divorced woman commits adultery ([ref:Matt 5:31-32|Matthew 5:31-32]).

Jesus answers the Pharisees' question about divorce by pointing back to the creation order and states that whoever divorces his wife for any reason other than sexual immorality and marries another commits adultery ([ref:Matt 19:3-9|Matthew 19:3-9]).

Mark's parallel to Jesus' teaching on divorce, where Jesus declares that whoever divorces his wife and marries another commits adultery against her, and likewise if a woman divorces her husband ([ref:Mark 10:2-12|Mark 10:2-12]).

The Old Testament provision regarding certificates of divorce to which Jesus responds. The Mosaic law allowed a man to give his wife a certificate of divorce, but Jesus tightens this regulation ([ref:5 Mos 24:1-4|Deuteronomy 24:1-4]).

The Mosaic law on adultery: "If a man commits adultery with another man's wife …" – the background for why Jesus uses the term μοιχεύει (commits adultery) in his teaching on divorce and remarriage ([ref:3 Mos 20:10|Leviticus 20:10]).

The creation order that a man shall leave his father and mother and be joined to his wife, and the two shall become one flesh – the theological basis for Jesus' teaching on the indissolubility of marriage ([ref:1 Mos 2:24|Genesis 2:24]).

Paul continues Jesus' command that a wife should not separate from her husband, and if she does, she must remain unmarried or be reconciled to her husband. Likewise, a man should not divorce his wife ([ref:1 Kor 7:10-11|1 Corinthians 7:10-11]).

Paul uses the marriage law as an illustration: a married woman is bound to her husband as long as he lives, and is called an adulteress if she becomes another man's while her husband is still alive ([ref:Rom 7:2-3|Romans 7:2-3]).
The prophet Malachi testifies that the Lord hates divorce and urges the Israelites to remain faithful to the wife of their youth ([ref:Mal 2:14-16|Malachi 2:14-16]).
